title.zh: 卷三百〇四 列傳第六十三 周渭 梁鼎 范正辭 劉師道 王濟 方偕 曹穎叔 劉元瑜 楊告 趙及 劉湜 王彬 仲簡
title.en: Volume 304 Biographies 63: Zhou Wei, Liang Ding, Fan Zhengci, Liu Shidao, Wang Ji, Fang Xie, Cao Yingshu, Liu YuanYu, Yang Gao, Zhao Ji, Liu Shi, Wang Bin, Zhong Jian
title.raw: 卷三百〇四 列傳第六十三 周渭 梁鼎 范正辭 劉師道 王濟 方偕 曹穎叔 劉元瑜 楊告 趙及 劉湜 王彬 仲簡 Volume 304 Biographies 63: Zhou Wei, Liang Ding, Fan Zhengci, Liu Shidao, Wang Ji, Fang Xie, Cao Yingshu, Liu YuanYu, Yang Gao, Zhao Ji, Liu Shi, Wang Bin, Zhong Jian

sentences.zh: 周渭，字得臣，昭州恭城人。

translations.literal: Zhou Wei, styled Dechen, was a native of Gongcheng in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wei, whose style name was Dechen, came from Gongcheng in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，養於諸父。

translations.literal: Orphaned in childhood, he was raised by his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents young and was brought up by his father's brothers.

sentences.zh: 力學，工為詩。

translations.literal: He studied diligently and excelled at composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to learning and was skilled at writing verse.

sentences.zh: 劉鋹據五嶺，昭州皆其地也，政繁賦重，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Liu Chang held the Five Ridges; all of Zhaozhou was his territory. Government was oppressive and taxes heavy; the people could barely live.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang controlled the Five Ridges, and Zhaozhou lay entirely within his domain. Administration was burdensome and levies crushing, until the people could scarcely survive.

sentences.zh: 渭率鄉人六百逾嶺，將避地零陵。

translations.literal: Wei led six hundred fellow townsmen across the mountains, intending to relocate to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei led six hundred men from his district over the ranges, planning to take refuge in Lingling.

sentences.zh: 未至，賊起，斷道絕糧，復還恭城，則廬舍煨燼，遂奔道州。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, bandits rose, blocking the roads and cutting off provisions. They returned to Gongcheng, but the houses had been burned to ash, so they fled to Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, rebels rose up, the roads were cut, and food ran out. They turned back toward Gongcheng only to find the dwellings reduced to embers, and so they pressed on to Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 為盜所襲，渭脫身北上。

translations.literal: Robbers attacked them; Wei escaped and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits fell upon them, but Wei broke free and made his way north.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，至京師，為薛居正所禮。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Jianlong era, he reached the capital and was received with courtesy by Xue Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong reign he reached the capital, where Xue Juzheng treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 上書言時務，召試，賜同進士出身，解褐白馬主簿。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on state affairs, was summoned for examination, and was granted the status of tong jinshi chushen; he took his first post as registrar of Baima.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne on current affairs, was called in for an examination, and was granted status as a tong jinshi; he then left office robes behind to serve as registrar of Baima.

sentences.zh: 縣大吏犯法，渭即斬之。

translations.literal: A senior clerk of the county violated the law; Wei immediately executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a senior clerk in the county broke the law, Wei had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 上奇其才，擢右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his talent and promoted him to Right Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his ability and promoted him to Right Palace Companion.

sentences.zh: 時魏帥符彥卿專恣，朝廷選常參官強幹者蒞其屬邑，以渭知永濟縣。

translations.literal: At the time the Wei military commissioner Fu Yanqing was domineering and arbitrary; the court selected a strong and capable regular official to take charge of one of his subordinate counties, and made Wei magistrate of Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of Wei, ruled with arrogant license, so the court chose a forceful regular official to govern one of his subordinate counties and appointed Wei magistrate of Yongji.

sentences.zh: 彥卿郊迎，渭揖於馬上，就館始與相見，略不降屈。

translations.literal: Yanqing came out to the suburbs to welcome him; Wei bowed from horseback and only met him face to face in the guest lodge, barely showing any deference.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing came out to greet him beyond the walls, but Wei merely bowed from the saddle and did not meet him properly until he reached the lodge, showing scarcely any deference.

sentences.zh: 縣有盜傷人而逸，渭捕獲，並暴廋匿者按誅之，不以送府。

translations.literal: A bandit in the county had wounded someone and fled; Wei captured him and also exposed and executed those who had harbored him, without turning them over to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: When a robber in the county wounded someone and fled, Wei seized him, exposed those who had hidden him, and punished them all by law without sending the case up to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，通判興州。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era, he served as vice-prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande reign he served as vice-prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 州領罝口砦多戍兵，監軍敖很，縱其下為暴，居人苦之。

translations.literal: The prefecture controlled Zykou Stockade, which had many garrison troops; the military supervisor was arrogant and fierce and allowed his subordinates to commit violence; the residents suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture oversaw Zykou Stockade, where many troops were stationed. The army supervisor was overbearing and let his men run wild, to the great misery of the local people.

sentences.zh: 渭馳往諭以禍福，斬其軍校，眾皆懾服。

translations.literal: Wei rushed there and explained the consequences to them, executed the military officers, and the masses all submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Wei hurried there, warned them of the consequences, beheaded their officers, and the troops all submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 詔書嘉獎，命兼本砦鈐轄。

translations.literal: An imperial edict praised and rewarded him and ordered him to concurrently hold the post of commander of that stockade.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict commended him and appointed him concurrently to command that stockade.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年，鳳州七房冶主吏盜隱官銀，擇渭往代。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaibao, the chief clerk of the Qifangye smeltery in Fengzhou embezzled official silver; Wei was chosen to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaibao the chief clerk at the Qifangye smeltery in Fengzhou concealed stolen official silver, and Wei was selected to take his place.

sentences.zh: 周歲，羨課數倍，賜緋魚，又遷知棣州。

translations.literal: Within a year, surplus revenue increased severalfold; he was granted scarlet robes and fish insignia, and was further transferred to govern Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the surplus in tax receipts had multiplied several times over. He was granted scarlet robes and fish insignia, and was soon transferred to govern Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 殿直傅延翰為監軍，謀作亂走契丹，為部下所告，渭擒之以聞；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fu Yanhan served as military supervisor and plotted to rebel and flee to Khitan; he was reported by his subordinates, and Wei captured him and reported it;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanhan, a palace attendant serving as army supervisor, plotted rebellion and flight to the Khitan; his subordinates informed on him, and Wei seized him and reported the matter;

sentences.zh: 命械至闕下，鞫得實，斬於西市。

translations.literal: He was ordered shackled to the capital; the investigation found the facts, and he was executed at the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered brought to the capital in fetters; the inquiry established the facts, and he was executed at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 渭在郡以簡肅稱，及還，吏民遮道泣留，俄詔賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: Wei was known in the prefecture for his austerity; when he returned, officials and people blocked the road weeping and begging him to stay. Soon an edict granted one million cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture Wei was known for his severity and restraint. When he left, officials and commoners blocked the road in tears, begging him to remain; soon an edict granted him a million cash.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，為廣南諸州轉運副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, he became vice commissioner of the transport circuit for the Guangnan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was made vice transport commissioner for the Guangnan circuits.

sentences.zh: 初，渭之入中原，妻子留恭城。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei had entered the Central Plains, his wife and children remained in Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei had first gone north into the Central Plains, his wife and children had remained behind in Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，平廣南，詔昭州訪求，賜錢米存恤之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, when Guangnan was pacified, an edict ordered Zhaozhou to seek them out and granted cash and grain for their support.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao, after Guangnan was pacified, an edict directed Zhaozhou to search for them and granted cash and grain for their relief.

sentences.zh: 及是，渭始還故里，鄉人以為榮。

translations.literal: By this time Wei was able to return to his native place for the first time; his fellow townsmen regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Now, for the first time, Wei was able to return home, and his neighbors took it as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 渭奏去劉鋹時稅算之繁者，重定田賦，興學校。

translations.literal: Wei memorialized to abolish the heavy taxes and levies from Liu Chang's time, to reestablish land tax assessments, and to establish schools.
translations.idiomatic: Wei memorialized to remove the heavy taxes and assessments left from Liu Chang's rule, to fix land levies anew, and to establish schools.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Inside Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Inside Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 屬有事交阯，主將逗撓無功。

translations.literal: At the time there was trouble with Jiaozhi; the commander was dilatory and achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: At the time hostilities had broken out with Jiaozhi, and the commanding general dallied without success.

sentences.zh: 有二敗卒擐甲先至邕州市，奪民錢，渭捕斬之。

translations.literal: Two defeated soldiers arrived at Yongzhou City ahead of the main force wearing armor and seized the people's money; Wei captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Two routed soldiers in armor reached Yongzhou City ahead of the army and robbed the people; Wei seized and executed them.

sentences.zh: 後至者悉令解甲以入，訖無敢犯。

translations.literal: Those who arrived later were all made to remove their armor before entering; in the end none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: All who came after were ordered to lay aside their armor before entering, and in the end none dared transgress.

sentences.zh: 移書交阯，諭朝廷威信，將刻日再舉。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Jiaozhi explaining the court's authority and prestige, stating that a new campaign would be launched on a set date.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a dispatch to Jiaozhi setting forth the court's authority and warning that another campaign would be mounted on a fixed day.

sentences.zh: 黎桓懼，即遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Li Huan was afraid and immediately sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was frightened and at once sent envoys to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 就加監察御史，在嶺南凡六年。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to Investigating Censor and spent six years in all in the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Investigating Censor and spent six years in all in the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 徙知揚州，進殿中侍御史，改兩浙東、西路轉運使，入為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Yangzhou, advanced to Palace Attendant Inside Censor, changed to transport commissioner for the Eastern and Western circuits of the Two Zhejiangs, and entered the capital as salt and iron judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Yangzhou, promoted to Palace Attendant Inside Censor, made transport commissioner for the eastern and western circuits of the Two Zhes, and then entered the capital as judicial commissioner of the Salt and Iron Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，曆判戶部、度支二勾院，出知亳州，賜金紫，俄換宋州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Censor, successively served as judicial officer of the Revenue and Expenditure Bureaus, went out to govern Bozhou, was granted gold and purple robes, and soon was transferred to Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Censor, served in turn as judicial officer of the Revenue and Expenditure Bureaus, went out to govern Bozhou, was granted gold and purple insignia, and soon was transferred to Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 加職方員外郎，為益州轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office and made transport commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Personnel and appointed transport commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 坐從子違詔市馬，黜為彰信軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Because his nephew violated an edict by purchasing horses, he was demoted to vice military commissioner of Zhangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because his nephew had violated an edict by buying horses, he was demoted to vice military commissioner of Zhangxin Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，真宗聞其清節，召還，將復用，詔下而卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, Zhenzong heard of his integrity and summoned him back, intending to reuse him, but the edict was issued and he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping, Zhenzong heard of his integrity, recalled him, and was about to employ him again, but the edict had scarcely been issued when he died, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 上閔其貧不克葬，賻錢十萬，以其子建中為乘氏主簿。

translations.literal: The emperor sympathized that he was too poor for burial and granted one hundred thousand in funeral funds, and made his son Jianzhong registrar of Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying his poverty and inability to afford burial, granted one hundred thousand in funeral funds and appointed his son Jianzhong registrar of Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 渭妻莫荃，賢婦人也。

translations.literal: Wei's wife Mo Quan was a virtuous woman.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's wife, Mo Quan, was a woman of exemplary virtue.

sentences.zh: 渭北走時，不暇與荃訣，二子孩幼，荃尚少，父母欲嫁之。

translations.literal: When Wei fled north he had no time to take leave of Quan; his two sons were still infants and Quan was still young; her parents wished to remarry her.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei fled north he had no chance to bid Quan farewell. Their two sons were still small, and Quan herself was young; her parents wished to marry her off again.

sentences.zh: 荃泣誓曰：「渭非久困者，今違難遠適，必能自奮。

translations.literal: Quan wept and swore: "Wei is not one to remain in hardship long; now in fleeing far in crisis he will surely be able to strive on his own."
translations.idiomatic: Quan wept and vowed: "Wei is not a man to remain long in hardship. Though he flees far in peril now, he will surely make his way."

sentences.zh: 」於是親蠶績碓舂，以給朝夕，二子皆畢婚娶。

translations.literal: Thereupon she personally raised silkworms and beat grain with a pestle to supply daily needs, and both sons were married in full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she raised silkworms herself, spun thread, and pounded grain to meet their daily needs, and saw both sons through marriage in full.

sentences.zh: 凡二十六年，復見渭，時人異之。

translations.literal: For twenty-six years in all she saw Wei again; people of the time found it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-six years in all she saw Wei again, and people of the day marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 朱昂著《莫節婦傳》紀其事。

translations.literal: Zhu Ang wrote "The Biography of Lady Mo the Chaste Woman" to record this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ang wrote The Biography of Lady Mo the Chaste Woman to commemorate her story.

sentences.zh: 梁鼎，字凝正，益州華陽人。

translations.literal: Liang Ding, styled Ningzheng, was a native of Huayang in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ding, whose style name was Ningzheng, was a native of Huayang in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖鉞，仕蜀為劍門關使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qian served Shu as commissioner of the Jianmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian had served Shu as commissioner of Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 父文獻，乘氏令。

translations.literal: His father Wengxian was magistrate of Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wengxian had been magistrate of Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 鼎，太平興國八年進士甲科，解褐大理評事、知秭歸縣，再遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Ding, in the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, passed the jinshi examination in the top grade; he took his first post as second-class section member of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Zigui, and was twice promoted to Assistant Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo Ding passed the jinshi examination in the top grade, took his first post as reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Zigui, and was twice promoted to Assistant Archivist.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，獻《聖德徽號頌》萬餘言，試文，遷殿中丞、通判歙州，以能聲聞，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he presented "Ode to the Sagely Virtue and August Designation" of more than ten thousand characters, was examined in literary composition, and was promoted to Palace Inside Gentleman and vice-prefect of Shezhou; because of his reputation for ability, there was an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign he presented an ode of more than ten thousand characters in praise of the sage virtue and august designation, underwent a literary examination, and was promoted to Palace Inside Gentleman and vice-prefect of Shezhou; his reputation for ability won an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 徙知吉州，民有蕭甲者，豪猾為民患，鼎暴其凶狀，杖脊黥面徙遠郡。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Jizhou; among the people was one Xiao Jia, overbearing and cunning, a menace to the people; Ding exposed his brutal conduct, flogged his back, tattooed his face, and exiled him to a distant prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to govern Jizhou, he found among the people a man named Xiao Jia, overbearing and cunning, a scourge to the district. Ding exposed his crimes, had his back flogged and his face tattooed, and exiled him to a distant prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗尤賞其強幹，代還，賜緋魚，舊例當給銀寶瓶帶，太宗特以犀帶賜之，記其名於御屏。

translations.literal: Taizong especially appreciated his toughness; when he returned on replacement, he was granted scarlet robes and fish insignia. By old precedent he should have received a silver precious-vase belt, but Taizong specially granted him a rhinoceros-horn belt and recorded his name on the imperial screen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong especially valued his forcefulness. When he returned on rotation he was granted scarlet robes and fish insignia. By precedent he should have received a silver precious-vase belt, but Taizong personally gave him a rhinoceros-horn belt instead and entered his name on the imperial screen.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，上言曰：「《書》云：『三載考績，三考黜陟幽明。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he memorialized: "The Book says: 'After three years examine the merits, and after three examinations dismiss the dark and promote the bright.'"
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era he memorialized: "The Book of Documents says: 'After three years examine merit; after three examinations dismiss the incompetent and promote the capable.'"

sentences.zh: 』此乃堯、舜氏所以得賢人治天下也。

translations.literal: This was how Yao and Shun obtained worthy men to govern all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is how Yao and Shun obtained worthy men to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 三代而下，典章尚存，兩漢以還，沿革可見。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties downward the institutions still survived; from the Two Han onward the evolution can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dynasties onward the institutions still survived, and from the Two Han the successive changes can be traced.

sentences.zh: 至於唐室，此道尤精，有考功之司，明考課之令，下自簿尉，上至宰臣，皆歲計功過，較定優劣，故人思激厲，績效著聞。

translations.literal: As for the Tang house, this method was especially refined: there was the Bureau of Merit Examination and clear regulations for merit assessment; from clerks and assistants up to chancellors, each year accomplishments and faults were reckoned and excellence and inferiority were determined, so people strove to be stimulated and achievements were conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang this practice was especially refined: there was a Bureau of Merit Examination and clear regulations for assessment. From clerks and assistants up to chancellors, each year merit and fault were reckoned and excellence and failure distinguished, so men strove to excel and achievements stood out.

sentences.zh: 五代兵革相繼，禮法陵夷，顧惟考課之文，祇拘州縣之輩，黜陟既異，名存實亡。

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties with successive wars saw rites and law in decline; as for the texts of merit examination, they only constrained officials of prefectures and counties; dismissal and promotion differed and the name survived while the substance perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties, with war upon war, saw rites and law decay. As for the texts on merit examination, they applied only to prefectural and county officials; promotion and demotion had lost their meaning, and the form survived without the substance.

sentences.zh: 且夫今之知州，即古之刺史，治狀顯著者，朝廷不知；

translations.literal: Moreover, today's prefectural governors are the ancient provincial governors; those whose governance was conspicuous—the court did not know;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, today's prefects are the ancient provincial governors. Those whose governance was outstanding—the court never learned of them;

sentences.zh: 方略蔑聞者，任用如故。

translations.literal: Those of whom strategy was unheard were employed as before.
translations.idiomatic: those of whom no strategy was ever heard were employed as before.

sentences.zh: 大失勸懲之理，浸成苟且之風。

translations.literal: This gravely lost the principle of encouragement and punishment and gradually formed a habit of lax compliance.
translations.idiomatic: This gravely betrayed the principle of reward and punishment and gradually bred a habit of lax compliance.

sentences.zh: 是致水旱薦臻，獄訟填溢，欲望天下承平，豈可得也。

translations.literal: Consequently floods and droughts came repeatedly, lawsuits overflowed—if one desired that the empire be at peace, how could it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Hence floods and droughts came in succession, lawsuits overflowed the courts—how could one hope for peace under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下繼二聖之丕圖，為億兆之司牧，念百官之未乂，思四海之未康，特詔有司，申明考績之法，庶幾官得其人，民受其賜矣。」

translations.literal: Bowing humbly, Your Majesty has succeeded the great design of the two sage emperors and is shepherd to the hundred millions; pondering that the hundred officials are not yet well governed and thinking that the four seas are not yet tranquil, specially decree the responsible officials to clarify the law of examining merits, so that perhaps officials will obtain the right men and the people will receive the benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has succeeded the great enterprise of the two sage emperors and is shepherd to the hundred millions. Pondering that the hundred officials are not yet well governed and that the four seas are not yet at peace, I beg that Your Majesty specially decree the responsible offices to clarify the law of merit examination, so that officials may be rightly chosen and the people receive its benefit."

sentences.zh: 俄為開封府判官，遷太常博士、三司右計判官，又為總計判官，會復三部，換度支判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was made judicial officer of the Kaifeng Prefecture, promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices and Right Calculator of the Three Bureaus, then aggregate calculator; when the three departments were restored he was exchanged to Expenditure judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture, promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices and Right Calculator of the Three Bureaus, then aggregate calculator; when the three departments were restored he was transferred to Expenditure judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 至道初，鼎洎陳堯叟建議興三白渠，及陳、許、鄧、穎、蔡、宿、亳數州用水利墾田，事具《食貨志》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, Ding together with Chen Yaosou proposed to revive the Sanbai Canal and use water conservancy to reclaim fields in Chen, Xu, Deng, Ying, Cai, Su, Bo and other prefectures—the matter is detailed in the Treatise on Food and Goods.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao reign Ding and Chen Yaosou proposed reviving the Sanbai Canal and using irrigation to reclaim land in Chen, Xu, Deng, Ying, Cai, Su, Bo, and several other prefectures; the matter is recorded in full in the Treatise on Food and Goods.

sentences.zh: 遷都官員外郎、江南轉運副使，就改起居舍人，徙陝西。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Court of the Imperial Clan and vice transport commissioner of the Jiangnan circuit, and was at once changed to Drafting Attendant and transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Court of the Imperial Clan and vice transport commissioner of Jiangnan, then at once made Drafting Attendant and transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二年，五將分道擊李繼遷，李繼隆擅出赤檉路無功，還奏軍儲失期，鼎坐削三任。

translations.literal: In the second year, five generals attacked Li Jiqian by separate routes; Li Jilong on his own went out the Chichan Road without success, returned and reported that military provisions had failed to arrive on schedule, and Ding was punished by demotion of three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year five generals attacked Li Jiqian by separate routes. Li Jilong on his own took the Chichan Road without success, then returned and reported that military provisions had failed to arrive on schedule; Ding was punished by demotion of three ranks.

sentences.zh: 復為殿中丞，領職如故。

translations.literal: He was restored as Palace Inside Gentleman and retained his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Palace Inside Gentleman and retained his duties as before.

sentences.zh: 以母老求郡，曆知徐、密二州。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested a prefectural post and successively governed Xu and Mi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly he requested a prefectural post and successively governed Xu and Mi.

sentences.zh: 真宗踐位，復舊官。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，遷兵部員外郎、知制誥，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of War and Drafting Attendant, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of War and Drafting Attendant, and was granted gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 時三司督逋負嚴急，有久被留係者，命鼎與薛映按籍詳定，多所蠲免。

translations.literal: At the time the Three Bureaus pressed urgently for collection of arrears; some had long been detained; the emperor ordered Ding and Xue Ying to examine the registers in detail, and many exemptions were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Three Bureaus pressed urgently for collection of arrears, and some had long been detained. The emperor ordered Ding and Xue Ying to examine the registers in detail, and many debts were remitted.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜右諫議大夫、度支使。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Right Remonstrance and Reviser and Expenditure Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he was appointed Right Remonstrance and Reviser and Expenditure Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時西鄙未寧，建議陝西禁解池鹽，所在官鬻，詔從之。

translations.literal: At the time the western border was not yet settled; he proposed that Shaanxi prohibit solution of pond salt and that officials sell it locally; the edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier was not yet settled. He proposed prohibiting private trade in salt from the Jiechi ponds in Shaanxi and having officials sell it locally; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 以鼎為製置使，楊覃為轉運使，張賀副之，又以內殿崇班杜承睿同製置鹽事。

translations.literal: Ding was made commissioner for the arrangement, Yang Tan transport commissioner, Zhang He his deputy, and Inner Palace Attendant of the Left Duty Du Chengrui was also made jointly responsible for salt affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was made commissioner for the arrangement, Yang Tan transport commissioner, Zhang He his deputy, and Inner Palace Attendant Du Chengrui was also appointed to oversee salt affairs jointly.

sentences.zh: 議者多言：「邊民舊食青鹽，其價甚賤。

translations.literal: Critics said many: "The border people formerly ate green salt, its price very low."
translations.idiomatic: Critics said repeatedly: "The border people have long eaten green salt, and its price is very low."

sentences.zh: 洎禁青鹽以困賊，令商賈入粟，運解鹽於緣邊，價直與蕃鹽不相遠，故蕃部齎鹽至者，不能貨鬻。

translations.literal: When green salt was prohibited to weaken the enemy and merchants were made to bring grain and transport solution salt to the border, the price was not far from Tibetan salt, so those of the frontier tribes who brought salt could not sell it.
translations.idiomatic: When green salt was banned to weaken the enemy and merchants were required to bring grain in exchange for government salt transported to the border, the price differed little from tribal salt, so tribesmen who brought salt could not sell it.

sentences.zh: 今若禁解池鹽，與內地同價，則民必冒禁復市青鹽，乃資盜糧也。

translations.literal: Now if pond salt from the solution pools is prohibited and sold at the same price as inland, the people will surely violate the prohibition and again buy green salt, thereby supplying grain to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: If Jiechi salt is now banned and sold at inland prices, the people will surely violate the prohibition and buy green salt again, thereby supplying grain to the bandits."

sentences.zh: 」時劉綜為陝西轉運使，鼎奏罷之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zong was Shaanxi transport commissioner; Ding memorialized to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Zong was Shaanxi transport commissioner; Ding memorialized to have him removed.

sentences.zh: 綜歸朝，亦密陳其非便。

translations.literal: Zong returned to court and also secretly stated its disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong returned to court he also secretly memorialized against the policy.

sentences.zh: 鼎既行，即移文禁止鹽商，所在約束乖當，延州劉廷偉、慶州鄭惟吉皆不從規畫。

translations.literal: After Ding had departed he immediately issued documents prohibiting salt merchants; the local constraints were improper; Yanzhou's Liu Tingwei and Qingzhou's Zheng Weiji both did not follow the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ding had set out he immediately issued documents prohibiting salt merchants, but the local restrictions were ill judged; Liu Tingwei of Yanzhou and Zheng Weiji of Qingzhou both refused to follow his plan.

sentences.zh: 又鼎奏運咸陽倉粟以實邊，粟已陳腐，鼎即與民，俟秋收易新粟，朝廷聞而止之，上封章密陳其煩擾者甚眾，鼎始謀多沮，遂令林特乘傳與永興張詠會鼎等同議可否，於是依舊通鹽商。

translations.literal: Again Ding memorialized to transport grain from the Xianyang granary to supply the border; the grain was already stale; Ding immediately gave it to the people and waited for the autumn harvest to exchange for new grain; the court heard of it and stopped it; memorials in sealed covers secretly stated its harassment in great numbers; many of Ding's initial plans were frustrated; the emperor ordered Lin Te to travel by fast relay and meet with Yongxing's Zhang Yong and Ding and others jointly to discuss feasibility; thereupon the former practice of allowing salt merchants was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Ding also memorialized to transport grain from the Xianyang granary to supply the border. The grain was already stale, and Ding at once distributed it to the people, intending to exchange it for new grain after the autumn harvest. When the court heard of this it halted the plan. Sealed memorials in great number complained of the harassment. Many of Ding's initial plans were thwarted, and the emperor ordered Lin Te to travel by fast relay to meet with Zhang Yong of Yongxing and Ding and others to discuss whether the policy should stand; thereupon the former practice of allowing salt merchants was restored.

sentences.zh: 鼎坐首議改作非是，詔罷度支使，守本官。

translations.literal: Ding was punished for being chief advocate of an improper change; an edict removed him as Expenditure Commissioner but let him retain his base rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was held responsible as chief advocate of an ill-advised change; an edict removed him as Expenditure Commissioner while letting him retain his base rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁內艱，起復。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his mother but was recalled to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his mother but was recalled from mourning to serve.

sentences.zh: 景德初，知三班院、通進銀台司兼門下封駁事，出知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he governed the Three-Ban Court and the Bureau for Forwarding Memorials and the Silver Terrace concurrently with gate seal and revision affairs, then went out to govern Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde reign he oversaw the Three-Ban Court and the Bureau for Forwarding Memorials and the Silver Terrace, concurrently handling gate seal and revision affairs, then went out to govern Fengxiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以居憂哭泣傷目，表求判西京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: Because mourning and weeping had injured his eyes, he submitted a memorial requesting appointment as judicial commissioner of the Western Capital retention office.
translations.idiomatic: Because mourning and weeping had injured his eyes, he memorialized requesting appointment as judicial commissioner of the Western Capital retention censorate.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年五十二，賜二子出身。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged fifty-two; his two sons were granted status as officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of fifty-two; his two sons were granted official status.

sentences.zh: 鼎偉姿貌，磊落尚氣，有介節，居官峻厲，名稱甚茂。

translations.literal: Ding had a imposing appearance, was upright and bold in spirit, had integrity, was stern in office, and his reputation flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Ding had a imposing bearing, was open and bold in spirit, possessed integrity, was stern in office, and enjoyed a flourishing reputation.

sentences.zh: 好學，工篆、籀、八分。

translations.literal: He loved learning and excelled at seal, zhuan, and bafen scripts.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at seal, large seal, and clerical scripts.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《隱書》三卷，《史論》二十篇，《學古詩》五十篇。

translations.literal: He once authored three fascicles of "Hidden Writings," twenty treatises of "Discussions on History," and fifty poems of "Studying Antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote three fascicles of Hidden Writings, twenty essays of Discussions on History, and fifty poems of Studying Antiquity.

sentences.zh: 子申甫、吉甫。

translations.literal: His sons were Shenfu and Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shenfu and Jifu.

sentences.zh: 范正辭

translations.literal: Fan Zhengci
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhengci

sentences.zh: 范正辭，字直道，齊州人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhengci, styled Zhidao, was a man of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhengci, whose style name was Zhidao, was a native of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父勞謙，獲嘉令。

translations.literal: His father Laoqian was magistrate of Huojia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Laoqian had been magistrate of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 正辭治《春秋公羊》、《穀梁》，登第，調補安陽主簿。

translations.literal: Zhengci studied the Gongyang and Guliang versions of the Spring and Autumn Annals, passed the examination, and was assigned as registrar of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengci studied the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, passed the civil examination, and was assigned as registrar of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，判入等，遷國子監丞、知戎州，改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era his judicial review entered the top grade; he was promoted to Gentleman of the Directorate of Education and magistrate of Rongzhou, and changed to Assistant Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign his examination placement entered the top grade; he was promoted to Gentleman of the Directorate of Education and magistrate of Rongzhou, then transferred to Assistant Archivist.

sentences.zh: 代還，治逋欠於淄州，轉運使稱其能，轉左讚善大夫，就知淄州。

translations.literal: When replaced and returned, he collected arrears in Zizhou; the transport commissioner praised his ability and he was transferred to Left Palace Companion and took charge of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from rotation he collected tax arrears in Zizhou; the transport commissioner praised his ability, and he was promoted to Left Palace Companion and appointed to govern Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，諸州部糧多不及期，正辭所部長山縣吏張秀督民輸，受錢二千，即杖殺之，郡中畏服。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Hedong, many prefectures failed to deliver grain on schedule; Zhengci's Changshan county clerk Zhang Xiu supervised the people in delivery, accepted two thousand cash, and Zhengci immediately had him beaten to death; the commandery submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Hedong, many prefectures failed to deliver grain on schedule. In Zhengci's jurisdiction the Changshan county clerk Zhang Xiu supervised the people's deliveries and accepted two thousand cash in bribes; Zhengci had him beaten to death on the spot, and the commandery submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，改殿中丞，通判棣、深二州，遷國子博士。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era he was changed to Palace Inside Gentleman, vice-prefect of Di and Shen prefectures, and promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he was made Palace Inside Gentleman and vice-prefect of Di and Shen, then promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉保勳奏充台直，會有言饒州多滯訟，選正辭知州事，至則宿係皆決遣之，胥吏坐淹獄停職者六十三人。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Baoxun memorialized to appoint him as a rectifier at court; at the time it was said Raozhou had many delayed lawsuits, and Zhengci was selected to manage the prefecture. On arrival he disposed of all long-detained cases, and sixty-three clerks were suspended for delaying cases in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Baoxun memorialized to appoint him as a court rectifier. At the time Raozhou was said to have many backlogged lawsuits, and Zhengci was chosen to manage the prefecture. When he arrived he cleared all long-pending cases, and sixty-three clerks were suspended for keeping prisoners too long.

sentences.zh: 會詔令料州兵送京師，有王興者，懷土憚行，以刃故傷其足，正辭斬之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered mustering prefectural troops to send to the capital. There was one Wang Xing who, attached to his homeland, feared the journey and deliberately wounded his foot with a blade; Zhengci executed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered prefectural troops mustered and sent to the capital. A man named Wang Xing, unwilling to leave home, deliberately wounded his foot with a blade; Zhengci had him executed.

sentences.zh: 興妻詣登聞上訴，太宗召見，正辭廷辨其事。

translations.literal: Xing's wife went to present an appeal at the Palace of Direct Appeal; Taizong summoned and met her, and Zhengci debated the matter in court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xing's wife appealed at the Palace of Direct Appeal. Taizong summoned her for an audience, and Zhengci argued the case before the court.

sentences.zh: 正辭曰：「東南諸郡，饒實繁盛，人心易動。

translations.literal: Zhengci said: "Among the prefectures of the southeast, Raozhou is truly flourishing and the people's hearts are easily stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengci said: "Among the southeastern prefectures, Raozhou is truly prosperous, and the people's hearts are easily stirred.

sentences.zh: 興敢扇搖，苟失控馭，則臣無待罪之地矣。

translations.literal: Xing dared to incite unrest; had I lost control, I would have had no place to await punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xing dared to incite disorder. Had I lost control, I would have had nowhere to await punishment."

sentences.zh: 」上壯其敢斷，特遷膳部員外郎，充江南轉運副使，賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his bold decisiveness, specially promoted him to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Rites, appointed him vice transport commissioner of Jiangnan, and granted five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his bold decisiveness, specially promoted him to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Rites, made him vice transport commissioner of Jiangnan, and granted five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 饒州民甘紹者，積財钜萬，為群盜所掠，州捕係十四人，獄具，當死。

translations.literal: Among the people of Raozhou was Gan Shao, who had amassed wealth of tens of millions and was plundered by a band of robbers; the prefecture arrested and bound fourteen men; the case was complete and they were to die.
translations.idiomatic: A Raozhou man named Gan Shao had amassed wealth in the tens of millions and was plundered by a band of robbers. The prefecture arrested fourteen men; the case was complete and they were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 正辭按部至，引問之，囚皆泣下，察其非實，命徙他所訊鞫。

translations.literal: When Zhengci arrived on inspection tour he summoned and questioned them; the prisoners all wept; perceiving the facts were not true he ordered them transferred elsewhere for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengci arrived on his inspection tour he summoned and questioned them. The prisoners all wept; seeing the case was false, he ordered them transferred elsewhere for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 既而民有告群盜所在者，正辭潛召監軍王願掩捕之。

translations.literal: Later someone reported where the band was; Zhengci secretly summoned the military supervisor Wang Yuan to make a surprise arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone reported where the bandits were. Zhengci secretly summoned the army supervisor Wang Yuan to make a surprise arrest.

sentences.zh: 願未至，盜遁去，正辭即單騎出郭二十里，追及之。

translations.literal: Before Yuan arrived the bandits fled; Zhengci at once rode out alone twenty li beyond the wall, pursued and overtook them.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wang Yuan arrived the bandits fled. Zhengci at once rode out alone twenty li beyond the city wall, pursued them, and overtook them.

sentences.zh: 賊控弦持肖來逼，正辭大呼，以鞭擊之，中賊雙目，執之。

translations.literal: The bandits drew bows and came pressing with blades; Zhengci shouted loudly and struck with his whip, hitting the bandit in both eyes, and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits drew their bows and advanced with blades drawn. Zhengci shouted and struck with his whip, hitting a bandit in both eyes, and seized him.

sentences.zh: 賊自刃不殊，餘賊渡江散走，追之不獲，旁得所棄贓。

translations.literal: The bandit killed himself but was not dead; the rest of the bandits fled across the river and scattered; they could not be caught, but by the way they recovered the abandoned booty.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit stabbed himself but was not killed. The rest fled across the river and scattered and could not be caught, but along the way they recovered the abandoned booty.

sentences.zh: 賊尚有餘息，正辭即載歸，令醫傅藥，創既愈，按其奸狀，伏法，而前十四人皆得釋。

translations.literal: The bandit still had breath; Zhengci at once loaded him and returned, ordered a doctor to apply medicine; when the wound healed he investigated his crimes and executed him by law, and the earlier fourteen all were released.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit still breathed. Zhengci at once brought him back, had a doctor treat him, and when the wound healed investigated his crimes and executed him by law; the earlier fourteen were all released.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，代歸，與洛苑副使綦仁澤、西京作坊副使尹宗諤同監折中倉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, on replacement he returned, and together with Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Parks Qi Renze and Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops Yin Zong'e jointly supervised the Zhongzhe Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong he returned on rotation and, together with Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Parks Qi Renze and Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops Yin Zong'e, jointly supervised the Zhongzhe Granary.

sentences.zh: 先是，令商人輸米豆而以茶鹽酬其直，謂之「折中」，復有言其弊，罷之，至是復置焉。

translations.literal: Earlier an order had merchants deliver rice and beans and be paid in tea and salt—called "zhongzhe"; again there was talk of its abuses and it was abolished; now it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier merchants had been required to deliver rice and beans and be paid in tea and salt—called "zhongzhe." Critics spoke of its abuses and it was abolished; now it was restored.

sentences.zh: 遷倉部員外郎，同知幕府州縣官考課，改判刑部，曆戶部、鹽鐵二判官，遷考功員外郎，通判定、揚、杭三州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Revenue, jointly managed merit examination of prefectural and county officials of the military commission, changed to judicial officer of the Ministry of Punishments, successively served as judicial officer of Revenue and Salt and Iron Bureaus, promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Personnel, and vice-prefect of Ding, Yang, and Hang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Revenue, jointly oversaw merit examination of prefectural and county officials under the military commission, transferred to judicial officer of the Ministry of Punishments, served in turn as judicial officer of the Revenue and Salt and Iron Bureaus, was promoted to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Personnel, and served as vice-prefect of Ding, Yang, and Hang.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷膳部郎中，召判三司勾院，俄復為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was promoted to Gentleman Inside the Office of the Ministry of Rites, summoned as judicial officer of the Three Bureaus Audit Office, and soon again Salt and Iron judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded he was promoted to Gentleman Inside the Ministry of Rites, summoned as judicial officer of the Three Bureaus Audit Office, and soon made Salt and Iron judicial officer again.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，出為河東轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he went out as Hedong transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he went out as Hedong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: In the third year, in his base office he concurrently served as Attendant Censor Managing Miscellaneous Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he concurrently served as Attendant Censor Managing Miscellaneous Affairs in his base office.

sentences.zh: 時李昌齡自忠武行軍起知梓州，董儼知壽州，王德裔、楊緘皆任轉運使，後失官宰畿邑。

translations.literal: At the time Li Changling from Zhongwu army march was raised to govern Zizhou, Dong Yan governed Shouzhou, Wang Deyi and Yang Jian all served as transport commissioners, then later lost office and governed capital suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Changling had risen from the Zhongwu army march to govern Zizhou; Dong Yan governed Shouzhou; Wang Deyi and Yang Jian had all served as transport commissioners, then later lost office and governed counties in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 正辭上言：「昌齡輩貪墨著聞，願陛下罷其民政。

translations.literal: Zhengci memorialized: "Changling and the rest are renowned for corruption; I beg Your Majesty to remove them from civil administration."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengci memorialized: "Changling and the others are notorious for corruption. I beg Your Majesty to remove them from civil administration."

sentences.zh: 」詔追還儼敕，餘悉代之。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Yan's appointment letter; the rest were all replaced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Dong Yan's appointment; the rest were all replaced.

sentences.zh: 又言：「治民之官，牧宰為急。

translations.literal: He also said: "Of officials who govern the people, pastoral administrators are most urgent."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Of officials who govern the people, pastoral administrators are the most urgent."

sentences.zh: 」舉吳奮等五人堪任大郡，復請令奮等各舉知縣、縣令，從之。

translations.literal: He recommended Wu Fen and four others competent for major prefectures, and further requested that Fen and the others each recommend county magistrates; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wu Fen and four others as fit to govern major prefectures, and further asked that Fen and the others each recommend county magistrates; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 坐鞫任懿獄，貶滁州團練副使。

translations.literal: He was punished for investigating the Ren Yi case and was demoted to vice military training commissioner of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for investigating the Ren Yi case and was demoted to vice military training commissioner of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復為倉部考功員外郎、通判鄆州，知淮陽軍，復膳部郎中，以年老，求監兗州商稅。

translations.literal: When amnesty came he was restored as Subordinate Section Member Outside the Offices of Revenue and Personnel merit examination, vice-prefect of Yanzhou, governed Huaiyang Army, restored to Gentleman Inside the Ministry of Rites; because of old age he requested to supervise Yanzhou commercial tax.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he was restored as Subordinate Section Member Outside the Offices of Revenue and Personnel for merit examination, vice-prefect of Yanzhou, and governor of Huaiyang Army, then restored to Gentleman Inside the Ministry of Rites; because of his age he requested to supervise Yanzhou commercial tax.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年四月卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 子識、諷，並進士及第。

translations.literal: His sons were Shi and Feng, both passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shi and Feng; both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 子 諷

translations.literal: Son Feng
translations.idiomatic: Son Feng

sentences.zh: 諷，字補之，以蔭補將作監主簿，獻《東封賦》，遷太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Feng, styled Buzhi, entered office by yin privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works, presented "Rhapsody on the Eastern Feng," and was promoted to Usher of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, whose style name was Buzhi, entered office by privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works, presented a rhapsody on the Eastern Feng, and was promoted to Usher of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 又獻所為文，召試入等，出知平陰縣。

translations.literal: He again presented his writings, was summoned for examination and entered the top grade, and went out as magistrate of Pingyin.
translations.idiomatic: He again presented his writings, was summoned for examination and placed in the top grade, and went out as magistrate of Pingyin.

sentences.zh: 會河決王陵埽，水去而土肥，失阡陌，田訟不能決，諷分別疆畔，著為券，民持去不復爭。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke at Wangling embankment, the water receded and the soil was rich but field boundaries were lost and land disputes could not be settled; Feng distinguished the boundaries, made deeds, and the people took them away without further quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Wangling embankment, the water receded and left rich soil, but field boundaries were lost and land disputes could not be settled. Feng distinguished the boundaries, drew up deeds, and the people took them away without further quarreling.

sentences.zh: 諷辨數激昂，喜為名聲，然亦操持在己，吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Feng was eloquent in debate and forceful in speech, liked to make a name, yet also held himself firm so clerks did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was eloquent and forceful in debate and liked to win renown, yet he also held himself strictly so clerks did not dare deceive him.

sentences.zh: 為縣存視貧弱，至豪猾大家，峻法治之。

translations.literal: In governing the county he cared for the poor and weak; toward powerful families and bullies he governed sternly.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the county he looked after the poor and weak, but toward powerful families and local bullies he applied stern law.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，遷大理評事、通判淄州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and was promoted to second-class section member of the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was promoted to reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲旱蝗，他穀皆不立，民以蝗不食菽，猶可藝，而患無種，諷行縣至鄒平，發官廩貨民。

translations.literal: In a year of drought and locusts other grain would not grow; the people because locusts do not eat beans could still plant them but feared having no seed; Feng went through the counties to Zouping and distributed from the government granary to loan the people.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of drought and locusts other grains would not grow. The people knew locusts do not eat beans and could still plant them, but feared having no seed. Feng went through the counties to Zouping and distributed grain from the government granary to loan the people.

sentences.zh: 縣令爭不可，諷曰：「有責，令無預也。

translations.literal: The county magistrate argued it could not be done; Feng said: "If there is blame, the magistrate need not be involved."
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate objected that it could not be done. Feng said: "If there is blame, the magistrate need not be involved."

sentences.zh: 」即出貸三萬斛；

translations.literal: At once he lent out thirty thousand hu;
translations.idiomatic: At once he lent out thirty thousand hu;

sentences.zh: 比秋，民皆先期而輸。

translations.literal: By autumn the people all paid ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn the people had all repaid ahead of schedule.

sentences.zh: 徙知梁山軍，以母老不行，得通判鄆州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Liangshan Army; because his mother was old he could not go and obtained vice-prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Liangshan Army, but because his mother was elderly he could not go and obtained the post of vice-prefect of Yanzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 時知州李迪貶衡州副使，宰相丁謂戒使者持詔書促上道，諷輒留迪數日，為治裝祖行。

translations.literal: At the time prefect Li Di was demoted to vice commissioner of Hengzhou; Chancellor Ding Wei warned the envoy to hold the edict and urge him on the road; Feng kept Di several days to prepare his baggage and give a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prefect Li Di was demoted to vice commissioner of Hengzhou. Chancellor Ding Wei instructed the envoy to press the edict and hurry him on the road. Feng kept Di several days to prepare his baggage and give him a farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 詔塞決河，州募民入芻揵，而城邑與農戶等，諷曰：「貧富不同而輕重相若，農民必大困。

translations.literal: An edict sealed the breach in the river; the prefecture recruited people to deliver fodder; city dwellers and farming households were treated alike; Feng said: "Rich and poor differ yet the burden is equal—the farmers will surely suffer greatly."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the river breach sealed. The prefecture recruited people to deliver fodder, treating city dwellers and farming households alike. Feng said: "Rich and poor differ, yet the burden is equal—the farmers will surely suffer greatly."

sentences.zh: 且詔書使度民力，今則均取之，此有司誤也。

translations.literal: Moreover the edict ordered measuring the people's strength, yet now it was levied equally—this is the fault of the office."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the edict ordered measuring the people's strength, yet now it is levied equally—this is the fault of the responsible office."

sentences.zh: 也。
」即改符，使富人輸三之二，因請下諸州以鄆為率，朝廷從其言。

translations.literal: At once he changed the warrant so the wealthy paid two-thirds, and requested that all prefectures take Yan as the standard; the court followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: At once he changed the warrant so the wealthy paid two-thirds, and requested that all prefectures take Yan as the standard; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 徙知廣濟軍，民避水堤居，凡給徭於官者，諷悉縱使護其家，奏除其租賦。

translations.literal: Transferred to govern Guangji Army; the people lived on flood dikes; for all who performed corvée for the government Feng let them stay to guard their homes and memorialized to exempt their rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to govern Guangji Army, he found the people living on flood dikes. For all who performed corvée for the government he let them stay to guard their homes and memorialized to exempt their rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常博士，以疾監舒州靈仙觀。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices; because of illness he supervised the Lingxian Abbey of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices; because of illness he was made supervisor of the Lingxian Abbey in Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尚御藥張懷德至觀齋祠，諷頗要結之，懷德薦於章獻太后，遂召還。

translations.literal: Zhang Huaide, who attended to imperial medicine, came to the abbey to perform sacrifices; Feng sought to cultivate ties with him; Huaide recommended him to Empress Zhangxian, and he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huaide, who attended to imperial medicine, came to the abbey to perform sacrifices. Feng sought to cultivate ties with him, and Huaide recommended him to Empress Zhangxian; he was then summoned back.

sentences.zh: 問所欲言，對曰：「今權臣驕悍，將不可製。

translations.literal: Asked what he wished to say, he replied: "Now the powerful ministers are arrogant and fierce and will soon be uncontrollable."
translations.idiomatic: Asked what he wished to say, he replied: "The powerful ministers are now arrogant and fierce and will soon be beyond control."

sentences.zh: 」蓋指曹利用也。

translations.literal: This referred to Cao Utilize.
translations.idiomatic: This referred to Cao Utilize.

sentences.zh: 利用貶，拜右司諫、三司度支判官。

translations.literal: When Utilize was demoted, Feng was appointed Right Secretariat Remonstrator and Expenditure judicial commissioner of the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Utilize was demoted, Feng was appointed Right Secretariat Remonstrator and Expenditure judicial commissioner of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 百官轉對，敕近臣閱視其可行者，類次以聞。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials took turns presenting policies, the edict ordered nearby officials to review what was feasible, classify them in order and report.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred officials took turns presenting policy proposals, an edict ordered nearby officials to review what was feasible, classify them, and report in order.

sentences.zh: 諷奏曰：「非上親覽決可否，則誰肯為陛下極言者。

translations.literal: Feng memorialized: "Unless Your Majesty personally reads and decides what is feasible or not, who will dare speak to the utmost for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized: "Unless Your Majesty personally reads and decides what is feasible, who will dare speak forthrightly for Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」玉清昭應宮災，下有司治火所起，諷曰：「此天之戒告，乃復置獄以窮治之，非所以應天也。

translations.literal: When the Yushan Zhaoying Palace burned, subordinates were ordered to investigate where the fire started; Feng said: "This is Heaven's warning and admonition—yet we again set up prisons to investigate exhaustively; this is not how to respond to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When the Yushan Zhaoying Palace burned, subordinates were ordered to investigate where the fire started. Feng said: "This is Heaven's warning, yet we set up prisons to investigate exhaustively—this is not how to respond to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」獄由是得解。

translations.literal: The prison case was thereby resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The prison case was thereby dismissed.

sentences.zh: 議者疑復修，諷上書諫：「山木已盡，人力已竭，宮必不成。

translations.literal: Critics doubted rebuilding; Feng memorialized in remonstrance: "The mountain timber is exhausted and human strength spent—the palace surely cannot be completed."
translations.idiomatic: Critics doubted rebuilding. Feng memorialized in remonstrance: "The mountain timber is exhausted and human strength spent—the palace cannot be completed."

sentences.zh: 臣知朝廷亦不為此，其如疑天下何。

translations.literal: I know the court also will not do this, but what of the doubt of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: I know the court will not do this either, but what of the doubts of all under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 宜詔示四方，使明知之。

translations.literal: An edict should be issued to the four quarters so all clearly know.
translations.idiomatic: An edict should be issued to the four quarters so that all may know clearly.

sentences.zh: 」於是下詔罷修。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued halting repair.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict was issued halting reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 改尚書禮部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Changed to Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Rites concurrently Attendant Censor Managing Miscellaneous Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Subordinate Section Member Outside the Office of the Ministry of Rites concurrently Attendant Censor Managing Miscellaneous Affairs.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演自許州來朝，圖相位，諷奏：「惟演嘗為樞密使，以皇太后姻屬罷之，示天下以不私，固不可復用。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan came to court from Xuzhou plotting for the chancellorship; Feng memorialized: "Weiyan once was Bureau Director of Military Affairs and was removed because of kinship with the Empress Dowager, showing the realm impartiality—he certainly cannot be reused."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan came to court from Xuzhou seeking the chancellorship. Feng memorialized: "Weiyan once served as Bureau Director of Military Affairs and was removed because of kinship with the Empress Dowager, showing the realm that the court is impartial—he certainly cannot be reused."

sentences.zh: 」遂以惟演守河南。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiyan was made defender of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weiyan was made defender of Henan.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，道過幽州北，見原野平曠，慨然曰：「此為戰地，不亦信哉。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Khitan; passing north of Youzhou he saw the open plains and sighed: "This is battleground—is it not so?"
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he passed north of Youzhou, saw the open plains, and sighed: "This is battleground—is it not so?"

sentences.zh: 」遼人相目不敢對。

translations.literal: The Liao people looked at one another and did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao people looked at one another and did not dare reply.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、知審刑院，出知青州，再遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Promoted to Attendant of the Heavenly Writings Pavilion and director of the Court of Judicial Review, went out to govern Qingzhou, again promoted to Gentleman Inside the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Heavenly Writings Pavilion and director of the Court of Judicial Review, went out to govern Qingzhou, and was again promoted to Gentleman Inside the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時山東饑，宰相王曾，青人，家積粟多，諷發取數千斛濟饑民，因請遣使安撫京東。

translations.literal: At the time Shandong suffered famine; Chancellor Wang Zeng, a man of Qing, had much grain stored; Feng had tens of thousands of hu taken to relieve the hungry and requested sending envoys to pacify Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shandong suffered famine. Chancellor Wang Zeng, a native of Qing, had much grain stored away. Feng had tens of thousands of hu taken to relieve the hungry and requested that envoys be sent to pacify Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 入為右諫議大夫、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered as Right Remonstrance and Reviser and acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Right Remonstrance and Reviser and acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 又請益漕江、淮米百萬，自河陽、河陰東下以賑貸之。

translations.literal: He again requested increasing transport of Jiang-Huai rice by one million, going down from Heyang and Heyin east to relief and loan.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested increasing transport of Jiang-Huai rice by one million hu, shipping it down from Heyang and Heyin eastward for relief and loans.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演倡議獻、懿二太后宜祔真宗廟室，諷彈奏之；

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan proposed that the two empresses Xian and Yi should be enshrined in Zhenzong's temple room; Feng impeached him;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan proposed that the two empresses Xian and Yi be enshrined in Zhenzong's temple room; Feng impeached him;

sentences.zh: 及言其在太后時權寵甚盛，且與後族連姻，請絀去。

translations.literal: and stated that in the Empress Dowager's time his power and favor were very great and he was allied by marriage with the empress's clan, requesting removal of his purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: and stated that during the Empress Dowager's time his power and favor had been very great and that he was allied by marriage with the empress's clan, requesting that his purple robe be removed.

sentences.zh: 仁宗不聽，諷袖告身以對曰：「陛下不聽臣言，臣今奉使山陵，而惟演守河南，臣早暮憂刺客。

translations.literal: Renzong would not listen; Feng took out his commission and replied: "Your Majesty does not heed my words; I am now going on mission to the imperial tombs while Weiyan guards Henan—I fear assassins morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong would not listen. Feng took out his commission and said: "Your Majesty does not heed my words. I am now going on mission to the imperial tombs while Weiyan guards Henan—I fear assassins morning and evening."

sentences.zh: 願納此，不敢復為御史中丞矣。

translations.literal: "I beg to surrender this and dare not again be Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: "I beg to surrender this and dare not again serve as Censor-in-Chief."

sentences.zh: 」帝不得已可之，諷乃趨出，遂貶惟演隨州。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to consent; Feng then hurried out and Weiyan was demoted to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to consent. Feng then hurried out, and Weiyan was demoted to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 陳堯佐罷參知政事，有王文吉者，告堯佐謀反，仁宗遣中官訊問，復以屬諷。

translations.literal: Chen Yaozuo was removed as Associate Administrator; one Wang Wenji reported Yaozuo plotted rebellion; Renzong sent a palace attendant to inquire and again entrusted it to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaozuo was removed as Associate Administrator. A man named Wang Wenji reported that Yaozuo plotted rebellion. Renzong sent a palace attendant to inquire and again entrusted the case to Feng.

sentences.zh: 夜中被旨究詰，旦得其誣狀奏之。

translations.literal: In the night he received orders for exhaustive interrogation; by dawn he obtained the false charges and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: In the night he received orders for exhaustive interrogation; by dawn he had obtained proof of the false charges and memorialized.

sentences.zh: 時上章懿皇后諡，宰相張士遜、樞密使楊崇勳日中不赴慰班，諷彈士遜與崇勳，俱罷。

translations.literal: At the time the posthumous title of Empress Zhangyi was being granted; Chancellor Zhang Shirun and Bureau Director Yang Chongxun did not come at noon to the condolence rotation; Feng impeached Shirun and Chongxun; both were removed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the posthumous title of Empress Zhangyi was being granted. Chancellor Zhang Shirun and Bureau Director Yang Chongxun did not attend the noon condolence rotation. Feng impeached Shirun and Chongxun, and both were removed.

sentences.zh: 諷嘗侍對，帝語及郭后亡子。

translations.literal: Feng once attended in audience; the emperor spoke of Empress Guo's deceased son.
translations.idiomatic: Feng once attended in audience when the emperor spoke of Empress Guo's deceased son.

sentences.zh: 諷言亡子大義當廢，陰合帝旨，以龍圖閣直學士權三司使。

translations.literal: Feng said the deceased son by great principle ought to be disowned; secretly it matched the emperor's intent; he was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagrams Hall and acting Three Bureaus Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said that by great principle the deceased son ought to be disowned—a view that secretly matched the emperor's intent—and he was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagrams Hall and acting Three Bureaus Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時狄棐為直學士已久，諷盛氣淩棐，宰相李迪右之，遂特詔班棐上，論者非之。

translations.literal: At the time Di Cai had been Direct Academician long; Feng with overbearing air looked down on Cai; Chancellor Li Di favored Feng; thereupon a special edict ranked Cai above—critics faulted this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Di Cai had long been Direct Academician. Feng with overbearing manner looked down on him, and Chancellor Li Di favored Feng; thereupon a special edict ranked Cai above him—critics faulted this.

sentences.zh: 尋轉閣學士，又疾免三司使，改翰林侍讀學士、管勾祥源觀。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Pavilion Academician; again because of illness relieved of Three Bureaus Commissioner; changed to Hanlin Palace Attendant Reader and overseer of Xiangyuan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Pavilion Academician; again because of illness he was relieved of the Three Bureaus Commissionership and made Hanlin Palace Attendant Reader and overseer of Xiangyuan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 徙會靈觀，復改閣學士、給事中、知兗州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Huiling Abbey; again changed to Pavilion Academician, Giving Huangmen Attendant, governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huiling Abbey, then again made Pavilion Academician, Giving Huangmen Attendant, and governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 既至郡，而龐籍為廣南東路轉運使，未行，上言：「向為侍御史，嘗奏彈諷以三司使曲為左藏監庫吳守則奏課遷官。

translations.literal: After reaching the prefecture, Pang Ji was Eastern Guangnan transport commissioner and had not yet departed; he memorialized: "Formerly as Attendant Censor I once impeached Feng for as Three Bureaus Commissioner bending the law to have Left Treasury Supervisor Wu Shouze memorialized for promotion by merit."
translations.idiomatic: After he reached the prefecture, Pang Ji was Eastern Guangnan transport commissioner and had not yet departed. He memorialized: "Formerly, as Attendant Censor, I once impeached Feng for, as Three Bureaus Commissioner, bending the law to have Left Treasury Supervisor Wu Shouze promoted by merit memorial."

sentences.zh: 尚美人同父弟娶守則女，諷以銀鞍勒遺守則相結納。

translations.literal: The younger brother by the same father of the Honored Beauty had married Shouze's daughter; Feng gave Shouze a silver saddle and bridle to form a connection.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Beauty's younger brother by the same father had married Shouze's daughter; Feng gave Shouze a silver saddle and bridle to form a connection.

sentences.zh: 既出兗州，乃紿言貧，假翰林白金器數千兩自隨，而增產於齊州，市官田虧平估。

translations.literal: After leaving Yanzhou he falsely claimed poverty and borrowed several thousand taels of Hanlin white gold vessels to take along, yet increased property in Qizhou, buying government fields in the prefecture below fair estimate."
translations.idiomatic: After leaving Yanzhou he falsely claimed poverty and borrowed several thousand taels' worth of Hanlin white-gold vessels to take with him, yet increased his property in Qizhou by buying government fields below fair estimate."

sentences.zh: 」置獄於南京劾之，諷坐方聽旨擅馳驛還兗州，當贖。

translations.literal: A prison was set up at Nanjing to investigate; Feng was punished for while awaiting orders rashly using the relay post to return to Yanzhou—liable to commutation.
translations.idiomatic: A case was set up at Nanjing to investigate. Feng was punished for rashly using the relay post to return to Yanzhou while awaiting orders—liable to commutation.

sentences.zh: 籍所奏有不實，當免官。

translations.literal: What Ji memorialized was partly untrue—he should be removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: What Pang Ji memorialized was partly untrue—he should be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 宰相呂夷簡嫉諷詭激，特貶諷武昌軍節度行軍司馬；

translations.literal: Chancellor Lü Yijian resented Feng's crafty sharpness and specially demoted Feng to military affairs secretary of Wuchang Army;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lü Yijian resented Feng's crafty sharpness and specially demoted Feng to military affairs secretary of Wuchang Army;

sentences.zh: 貸籍，止降官知臨江軍。

translations.literal: Ji was pardoned, only demoted to govern Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji was pardoned and only demoted to govern Linjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 由是宰相李迪等坐親善諷皆斥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chancellor Li Di and others for befriending Feng were all expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chancellor Li Di and others, for befriending Feng, were all expelled.

sentences.zh: 歲中徙保信軍，聽居舒州持母喪，又許歸齊州。

translations.literal: Mid-year transferred to Baoxin Army, permitted to live in Shuzhou while observing mourning for his mother, also permitted to return to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-year he was transferred to Baoxin Army, permitted to live in Shuzhou while observing mourning for his mother, and also permitted to return to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 日飲酒自縱，為時所譏。

translations.literal: He drank wine daily and indulged himself, and was ridiculed by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He drank wine daily and indulged himself, and was ridiculed by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 服除，改將作少監、知淮陽軍，遷光祿卿、知陝州，道改潞州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, changed to Vice Director of Imperial Works and governor of Huaiyang Army, promoted to Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia and governor of Shaanzhou, on the road changed to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Vice Director of Imperial Works and governor of Huaiyang Army, promoted to Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia and governor of Shaanzhou, and on the road was transferred to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 入見帝言：「元昊不可擊，獨以兵守要害，捍侵掠，久當自服。

translations.literal: On audience he told the emperor: "Yuan Hao cannot be attacked; only hold the army at strategic points, repel raids—in time he will submit of himself."
translations.idiomatic: On audience he told the emperor: "Yuan Hao cannot be attacked. Hold the army only at strategic points and repel raids—in time he will submit of himself."

sentences.zh: 倘內修百度，躬節儉，如祖宗故事，則疆事不足憂。

translations.literal: "If within you cultivate the hundred measures and personally practice frugality like the ancestors' precedents, then frontier affairs need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: "If within the court you cultivate the hundred measures and personally practice frugality as the ancestors did, then frontier affairs need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」復給事中，卒。

translations.literal: Restored to Giving Huangmen Attendant; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Giving Huangmen Attendant and died.

sentences.zh: 諷嘗建議朝廷當差擇能臣，留以代大臣之不稱職者。

translations.literal: Feng once proposed the court should select able ministers and retain them to replace ministers not fit for office.
translations.idiomatic: Feng once proposed that the court should select able ministers and keep them on hand to replace ministers unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 大臣聞而惡之。

translations.literal: The great ministers heard and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers heard of this and hated it.

sentences.zh: 又數短參知政事王隨於帝前，因奏：「外人謂臣逐隨將取其位，願先出臣，為陛下引奸邪去，而朝廷清矣。

translations.literal: He also several times belittled Associate Administrator Wang Sui before the emperor, and memorialized: "Outsiders say I expelled Sui to take his post—I beg first to send me out for Your Majesty to draw off wicked flatterers, and the court will be clear."
translations.idiomatic: He also several times belittled Associate Administrator Wang Sui before the emperor and memorialized: "Outsiders say I expelled Sui to take his post. I beg first to send me away so Your Majesty may draw off wicked flatterers, and the court will be clear."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗與張士遜議事不合，諷曰：「世謂大事未易可議，小事不足為，所為終何事邪？

translations.literal: He also once disagreed with Zhang Shirun in discussion; Feng said: "The age says great affairs are not easily debated and small affairs not worth doing—what in the end can be accomplished?"
translations.idiomatic: He also once disagreed with Zhang Shirun in discussion. Feng said: "People say great affairs are hard to debate and small affairs not worth doing—what in the end can be accomplished?"

sentences.zh: 」及為龐籍訟，人謂大臣陰諷籍焉。

translations.literal: When he sued for Pang Ji, people said the great ministers had secretly incited Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When he prosecuted Pang Ji, people said the great ministers had secretly incited Pang Ji.

sentences.zh: 諷類曠達，然捭闔圖進，不守名檢，所與遊者輒慕其所為，時號「東州逸黨」。

translations.literal: Feng resembled broad unconstrained conduct, yet schemed and maneuvered for advancement, did not observe propriety, those who associated with him always admired his deeds, and at the time they were called the "Eastern Region Unrestrained Clique."
translations.idiomatic: Du Feng seemed free-spirited and easygoing, yet he schemed and maneuvered for advancement and paid no heed to propriety. Those who kept company with him invariably admired his ways, and they were known at the time as the "Eastern Region Unrestrained Clique."

sentences.zh: 山東人顏太初作《逸黨詩》刺之，而薑潛者又嘗貽書以疏其過雲。

translations.literal: Yan Taichu of Shandong wrote "Poem on the Unrestrained Clique" to satirize them, and Jiang Qian also once sent a letter setting forth his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Taichu of Shandong wrote Poem on the Unrestrained Clique to satirize them, and Jiang Qian also once sent a letter laying out his faults.

sentences.zh: 子寬之，終尚書刑部郎中、知濠州。

translations.literal: His son Kuanzhi ultimately reached Director of the Penal Bureau in the Ministry of Justice and governed Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuanzhi eventually rose to Director of the Penal Bureau in the Ministry of Justice and served as prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 劉師道

translations.literal: Liu Shidao
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shidao

sentences.zh: 劉師道，字損之，一字宗聖，開封東明人。

translations.literal: Liu Shidao, styled Sunzhi, also styled Zongsheng, was a native of Dongming in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shidao, styled Sunzhi and also Zongsheng, was a native of Dongming in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父澤，右補闕。

translations.literal: His father Ze was Right Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ze served as Right Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 師道，雍熙二年舉進士，初命和州防禦推官，曆保寧、鎮海二鎮從事，凡十年。

translations.literal: Shidao passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi, was first appointed defense push officer of Hezhou, served successively as staff officer in the Baoning and Zhenhai commands, altogether ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi. He was first appointed defense push officer of Hezhou and then served as staff officer in the Baoning and Zhenhai commands for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 王化基、呂祐之、樂史薦於朝，擢著作佐郎，才一月，會考課，又遷殿中丞，出知彭州，就加監察御史。
